data.title: Isoniazid (INH)
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Isonicotinic acid hydrazide; first-line antituberculous drug
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Isonicotinic acid hydrazide; first-line antituberculous drug

## Mechanism of action
- Prodrug activated by mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase (KatG)
- Inhibits InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase) → blocks mycolic acid synthesis in the cell wall
- Bactericidal for rapidly dividing bacilli; bacteriostatic for resting ones

## Pharmacokinetics
- Well absorbed; penetrates all tissues and caseous material
- Metabolised by N-acetylation (NAT2) — slow acetylators (about half of Indians) have more neuropathy; fast acetylators more hepatitis (debated)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- All forms of TB including cutaneous TB (lupus vulgaris, scrofuloderma, TBVC, tuberculids)
- Latent TB infection before biologics/JAK inhibitors (6–9 months alone, or with rifapentine/rifampicin in short regimens)

## Dose & formulations
- 5 mg/kg/day (max 300 mg) in fixed-dose combinations (India NTEP weight bands)
- Pyridoxine 10–25 mg/day to prevent neuropathy (higher in HIV, diabetes, malnutrition, pregnancy, alcoholism)

## Adverse effects
- Hepatitis (age-related; higher with rifampicin, alcohol)
- Peripheral neuropathy (pyridoxine deficiency) — prevented by pyridoxine
- Pellagra (niacin deficiency) — photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia
- Drug-induced lupus (ANA, antihistone antibodies)
- Acneiform eruption, exfoliative dermatitis, DRESS; optic neuritis, seizures, psychosis (rare)

## Contraindications
- Previous INH-induced hepatitis; acute liver disease

## Drug interactions
- Inhibits CYP2C19/3A4 → raises phenytoin and carbamazepine levels
- Antacids reduce absorption; alcohol adds hepatotoxicity

## Monitoring
- LFT at baseline and if symptoms (routine in high-risk); ask about neuropathy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy with pyridoxine.

## Viva points
- Give pyridoxine with INH
- Cutaneous side effects: pellagra, acneiform eruption, drug-induced lupus
- Slow acetylators → neuropathy

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7 (Antituberculous agents); Wolverton 4e ch.9 and ch.26 (TB screening before biologics). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
